is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles funestus, a major malaria vector.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping of CYP6M7, CYP6P9a, and CYP6P9b, which are listed as tier 2 markers for An. funestus.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports haplotype diversity, number of polymorphic sites, and haplotype frequencies for CYP6M7, CYP6P9a, and CYP6P9b in field populations (e.g., page 12, 'Genetic variability of candidate resistance genes in relation to pyrethroid resistance'; page 13, Figure 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Mbinga (Zambia), Chikwawa District (Malawi), and Tihuquine (Mozambique) (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study conducting bioassays, microarray, and sequencing on field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper provides specific locations: Mbinga (Katete District, Zambia), Chikwawa District (Malawi), and Tihuquine (Chokwe District, Mozambique) (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the paper references previous work on the same populations (e.g., Riveron et al. 2013, Cuamba et al. 2010), this study presents new microarray and sequencing data for these populations.

supplement.evidence: The necessary data regarding genotype counts and frequencies are provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the molecular basis of pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles funestus populations from Zambia, Malawi, and Mozambique. It identifies CYP6M7 as a key resistance gene alongside the previously identified CYP6P9a and CYP6P9b, demonstrating that resistance in Zambia involves different evolutionary forces and a distinct resistance profile compared to Malawi and Mozambique.
